name: Trampoline / family entertainment center
summary: Indoor FEC (trampoline courts, ninja/climbing, soft play, arcade, party rooms, café) in a high-bay box — most often a converted big box or warehouse, sometimes a new pre-engineered building. Building cost is low per SF (simple shell, open floor); the attraction package (trampolines, play structures, ropes courses, games) is a large separate FF&E/equipment item. Values derived from RSMeans warehouse/retail shells (2019) and size data from Main Event; no franchise Item 7 table was retrieved in this session.

typicalSize.method: Trampoline/adventure parks commonly 20,000–45,000 SF (first Sky Zone 17,000 SF, e3); multi-attraction FECs like Main Event 37,500–78,000 SF (e4). Mid 35,000.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Box at ~0.2–0.35 FAR with ~5–8 spaces per 1,000 SF. Derived.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Commercial-recreation zoning typically 4–8 spaces per 1,000 SF; peak birthday-party loads. Derived.

perPrimaryUnit.method: 2025 dollars, building + interiors + on-site work, excluding attraction equipment. RSMeans 2019 hard cost warehouse $131/SF (e1) and retail store $151 union / $134 open shop (e2) → ≈ $170–195/SF in 2025 for a new masonry box; pre-engineered high-bay buildings are cheaper, so new-build mid ≈ $185 incl. site. Many FECs are conversions of existing boxes (~$60–100/SF for MEP, restrooms, party rooms, finishes, sprinkler upgrades). Mid $160 weights new-build and conversion; low $70 = conversion; high $275 = ground-up with mezzanines, high-end finishes.

scope.notes: Excludes trampolines/play structures/ropes courses/arcade games (lineItems), furniture, land, soft costs, off-sites, impact/tap fees.

qualityTiers.method: economy ≈ low/mid (70/160 = 0.44, raised to 0.6 as economy new-build); luxury = high/mid (275/160); premium interpolated.

systemSplit.method: Derived for a pre-engineered high-bay box: building system 13 ≈ 15%, slab 03 ≈ 11%, sprinklers 21 for high-piled/high-bay occupancy, HVAC for assembly loads 10%, party rooms/restrooms in 09/22. On-site work ≈ 6%. Not sourced.

lineItems.name: Trampoline courts, dodgeball, foam pit, ninja course (installed)

cost.method: Derived allowance per SF of attraction footprint; verify with park-equipment vendor quotes or franchise FDD Item 7 tables.
Derived allowance for a custom multi-level play structure.

lineItems.name: Ropes course / climbing walls / zip line

cost.method: Same basis as entertainment-venue arcade-games line item.
Derived: ~300–400 SF rooms with finishes, lighting, AV.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Café furniture, lockers, cubbies, POS, signage (attractions separate). Derived.

pctOfHard.method: Simple box design (RSMeans model architectural fee ~7%) plus MEP, permits, attraction engineering/inspections. Derived.

softCosts.notes: Franchise systems add franchise fees; amusement-device inspections/permits vary by state.

hard.method: Conversions of existing boxes carry higher field risk.

perPrimaryUnit.method: low 70×1.1 to high 275×1.22; excludes attraction equipment.
